item.title: TopCon: A Hyperbolic Theme-Aware GNN for Hierarchical and Semantic Representation in Knowledge Graphs
item.description: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) serve as powerful tools for representing and reasoning over complex relational data. However, existing KG embedding methods in Euclidean space often struggle to capture inherent hierarchical structures (e.g., “Animal$\rightarrow$→ Mammal$\rightarrow$→ Cat”) and latent semantic themes (e.g., “Biology” vs. “Physics”), due to their geometric limitations of Euclidean spaces in modeling multi-level relations and handling node distribution imbalance. To overcome these limitations, we propose TopCon, a novel hyperbolic Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework designed to models multi-level relationships among themes, concepts, and entities in KGs while mitigating node distribution imbalance. TopCon leverages inclusion constraints between the hyperbolic concept spheres to represent capture hierarchical relations, and it improves global semantic representations by generating latent topics from entities and concepts. Local nodes obtain global topic distributions through neighbor-aware message passing, which are then integrated into the hyperbolic GNN to reduce node sparsity. Extensive experiments on WN18RR, FB15k-237, and YAGO3-10 demonstrate that TopCon outperforms state-of-the-art geometric baselines, achieving consistent gains on long-tail entities and superior hierarchical modeling accuracy, while maintaining competitive overall performance.
item.authors: Jianping Zhu;Jinsong Chen;Kun He;

item.title: A Qubit-Inspired Artificial Flora Optimization Algorithm for Efficient Feature Selection
item.description: Feature selection plays a critical role in optimizing machine learning models by reducing dimensionality, improving classification performance, and enhancing computational efficiency. This study proposes the Adaptive Quantum Flora Feature Selection (AQFFS) algorithm, which combines artificial flora-inspired growth dynamics with quantum probability-based transitions to identify compact and informative feature subsets. Structured refinement is achieved through root, stem, and leaf growth phases, while Hadamard and Pauli-X quantum gates introduce probabilistic transitions that balance exploration and exploitation. AQFFS was evaluated on 16 benchmark datasets using both a Quantum Circuit-based classifier and the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifier to assess performance across quantum and classical paradigms. Comparative experiments against several state-of-the-art feature selection methods, including Artificial Flora Optimization (AFO), Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA), Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO), Improved Binary Manta Ray Foraging Optimization (IBMRFO), Fuzzy Fitness Memetic Algorithm with Tabu Search and Hill Climbing (FFMATSHC), and Fuzzy PSO with Greedy Forward Selection (FPGFS), demonstrated improvements in classification accuracy, feature subset reduction, and runtime efficiency. Ablation analysis highlighted the importance of both operator-inspired stochastic updates and biologically guided adaptation, while statistical significance testing confirmed the consistency of performance gains across datasets and classifiers. The results indicate that AQFFS provides a scalable and model-agnostic framework for high-dimensional feature selection, with applicability in both classical and quantum machine learning contexts.
item.authors: Keerthi Gabbi Reddy;Deepasikha Mishra;Ahmet Cevahir Çınar;

item.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Restricted Hopfield Networks
item.description: Restricted Hopfield Networks (RHNs) extend classical Hopfield neural networks by incorporating hidden layers and trainable retrieval dynamics, thereby improving storage capacity and stability. This work presents a systematic theoretical and empirical investigation of the adversarial robustness of RHNs. We analyze the Subspace Rotation Algorithm (SRA) and establish two theoretical results: SRA produces optimal semi-orthogonal weight matrices for RHNs, and these weight structures induce non-expansive retrieval dynamics that prevent adversarial perturbations from being amplified. We further identify two factors associated with robustness: the filtering effect of the learned signal subspace and gradient–pattern alignment (GPA). Our analysis indicates that semi-orthogonality and signal-subspace dimensionality play particularly important roles, whereas GPA serves as a complementary robustness indicator. We compare RHNs with Modern Hopfield Networks (MHNs) and Predictive Coding Networks (PCNs) on the Alphabet and Character datasets. Robustness is evaluated under masking, Gaussian noise, and transferred adversarial attacks generated by an independently trained autoencoder, including FGSM, FFGSM, MIFGSM, NIFGSM, BIM, PGD, EOTPGD, Jitter, and SPSA. Quantitative and qualitative results show that RHNs achieve the most consistent retrieval performance across corruption types and perturbation magnitudes. RHNs generally outperform MHNs and remain competitive with or superior to PCNs under transferred adversarial attacks. These results demonstrate that semi-orthogonal weight structures and limited signal subspaces provide RHNs with an effective and theoretically grounded defense against adversarial perturbations.
item.authors: Ci Lin;Tet Yeap;Iluju Kiringa;

item.title: CHASE: A Causal Hypergraph Based Framework for Root Cause Analysis in Multimodal Microservice Systems
item.description: In recent years, the widespread adoption of distributed microservice architectures across the industry has greatly increased the demand for improved system availability and robustness. Enterprise-level microservice systems often involve complex service invocation paths and system dependencies, making it challenging to quickly identify anomalies during service interactions, which inevitably hinders normal system operations and maintenance. In this paper, we propose CHASE—a Causal Hypergraph grAph baSed framEwork—for root cause analysis in microservice systems. CHASE is designed to handle multimodal data sources, including traces, logs, and system monitoring metrics. Specifically, CHASE begins by encoding each type of input data—such as traces, logs, and metrics—into representative embeddings. These embeddings are then integrated into a unified multimodal invocation graph that captures the relationships among services. Anomaly detection is subsequently applied to each service instance node through attentive heterogeneous message passing, leveraging contextual information from adjacent metric and log nodes. Finally, CHASE constructs a causal hypergraph, where hyperedges represent inferred causal relationships among anomalies, and utilizes this structure to accurately localize root causes within the microservice system. We evaluate the proposed framework on two public microservice datasets with distinct attributes and compare with seven benchmark methods. The results show that CHASE achieves the average performance gain up to 36.2%(A@1) and 29.4%(Percentage@1), respectively to its best counterpart.
item.authors: Ziming Zhao;Zhenwei Wang;Tiehua Zhang;Zhishu Shen;Hai Dong;Zhen Lei;Xingjun Ma;Gaowei Xu;Zhijun Ding;Yun Yang;

item.title: TypeBandit: Type-Level Context Allocation and Reweighting for Effective Attribute Completion in Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
item.description: Heterogeneous graphs are widely used to model multi-relational systems, but missing node attributes remain a major bottleneck for downstream learning. We identify and formalize type-dependent information asymmetry: the phenomenon that different node types provide substantially different levels of useful signal for attribute completion. Motivated by this observation, we propose TypeBandit, a lightweight, model-agnostic methodology for heterogeneous attribute completion. TypeBandit combines topology-aware initialization, type-level bandit sampling, and joint representation learning. It allocates a finite global sampling budget across node types, samples representative nodes within each type, and uses the resulting sampled type summaries as shared contextual signals during representation construction. By operating at the type level rather than over each target node’s local neighborhood, TypeBandit keeps the adaptive state compact and computationally practical for large heterogeneous graphs. A key advantage of TypeBandit is architectural flexibility. Rather than requiring a new heterogeneous graph neural network architecture, TypeBandit acts as a type-aware front end that can be integrated with representative heterogeneous GNN backbones, including R-GCN, HetGNN, HGT, and SimpleHGN. We further introduce a hybrid pretraining scheme that combines structural degree priors with feature propagation, yielding a more reliable initializer than degree-only pretraining. Under a fixed-split protocol on DBLP, IMDB, and ACM, TypeBandit provides dataset-dependent but practically meaningful gains, with the clearest improvements on DBLP, more modest gains on ACM, and initialization-sensitive behavior on IMDB. Additional ablation, stability, efficiency, semantic-propagation, and sampled OGBN-MAG experiments further support TypeBandit as a practical strategy for heterogeneous attribute completion when type-specific information is unevenly distributed and sampling resources are limited.
item.authors: Ta-Yang Wang;Rajgopal Kannan;Viktor Prasanna;

item.title: Internal and External Verification Assisted Deep Clustering Network for Unsupervised Multimodal Fake News Detection
item.description: The proliferation of fake news on social media platforms has evolved into a pervasive global societal issue. Its latent diffusion seriously distorts public perception and threatens the construction of the social trust system. Current fake news detection methods are highly dependent on manually annotated news data. However, social media information is characterized by real-time explosive nature and multimodal complexity, resulting in high annotation costs and poor timeliness of labels. To deal with the challenge of unsupervised multimodal fake news detection (UMFND), we propose an internal and external verification assisted deep clustering network (IEV-DCN) for UMFND, consisting of an internal and external verification (IEV) module, a joint optimization rectification (JOR) mechanism, and a density-based multimodal clustering (DMC) module. The IEV module contains an internal verification (IV) part and an external verification (EV) part. The IV part employs multi-grained cross-modal attention mechanism to evaluate image-text semantic alignment, while the EV part leverages external knowledge corpus to retrieve relevant evidence of news samples, and implements evidence-guided preliminary assessment via multimodal large language model (MLLM). The JOR mechanism uses image-text consistency to correct the confidence of preliminary assessment, and generates pseudo labels for samples based on the corrected confidence. Furthermore, the DMC module distinguishes the quality of samples based on their densities, and uses the generated pseudo labels to constrain clustering and enhance the clustering effect. Experiments on widely used fake news datasets have shown that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art fake news detection works.
item.authors: Fei Wu;Zhihang Sheng;Yimu Ji;Xiao-Yuan Jing;Guo-Ping Jiang;

item.title: GOWalker: Accelerating Large-Scale Second-Order Random Walks via CPU-GPU Collaboration
item.description: Second-order random walks (SORWs) capture higher-order graph structures via current-previous vertex transitions. Existing CPU-GPU heterogeneous systems, though optimized for first-order random walks, face two bottlenecks in SORWs: underutilized CPU resources due to GPU-centric designs, and low data transfer efficiency caused by frequent inter-block transitions. In this paper, we present GOWalker, a CPU-GPU collaborative system tailored for large-scale SORWs. First, we classify walk states into intra- and inter-block types. The GPU updates intra-block states and inter-block states whose required blocks are GPU-resident, whereas the CPU updates the remaining cross-device inter-block states. Second, we combine two coordinated policies: GPU-side walk-aware block scheduling selects blocks with the most updatable walks, while CPU-side column-first grid scheduling prioritizes inter-block walk states associated with GPU-resident blocks. Finally, a four-phase cooperative pipeline coordinates and overlaps block loading, walk loading, GPU computation, and CPU processing across iterations to improve resource utilization. Extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic graphs, including billion-scale graphs, show that GOWalker outperforms CGgraph, LightTraffic, and Het-SOWalker on both evaluated single-GPU server configurations, with average speedups ranging from 2.24× to 4.71×.
item.authors: Yutong Wu;Chengzhi Jing;Zhan Shi;Peng Fang;Wang Zhang;Renzhi Xiao;Fang Wang;Dan Feng;

item.title: More is Better: A Theoretical Framework for the Efficacy of Multi-Omics Data Integration
item.description: Integrating heterogeneous omics data is crucial for comprehending complex biological systems; however, the theoretical underpinnings of its empirical benefits over single-omics methodologies remain ambiguous. To address this gap, we introduce the “More is Better” theorem, which provides a theoretical rationale for the performance enhancements observed through multi-omics data integration. The fundamental intuition is that, within the adaptive weighting framework, the model’s hypothesis space can be broadened as additional omics data are integrated, potentially diminishing model risk. Nevertheless, we also highlight a significant constraint: the inclusion of noisy or marginally relevant omics may not enhance performance and could even result in deterioration. This underscores the underlying principle that expanding the hypothesis space does not inherently ensure a reduction in risk. Drawing on this principle, we propose Supervised Adaptive Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis (SASCCA), a scalable multi-omics integration approach that selectively accentuates informative omics types through adaptive weighting while enforcing sparsity for biomarker selection. We derive theoretical assurances of SASCCA’s superiority over single-omics models and present an efficient optimization algorithm with guaranteed convergence. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets corroborate our theoretical predictions and demonstrate the efficacy and robustness of SASCCA.
item.authors: Heng Zhang;Zhi-Ping Liu;

item.title: 3DMS-CTR: A Click-Through Rate Prediction Model Based on Feature Extraction Across Frequency, Topology, and Temporal Dimensions
item.description: Feature extraction and representation play a crucial role in click-through rate(CTR) prediction tasks. This work is inspired by multi-scale feature fusion techniques in computer vision. By integrating and fusing features extracted at different scales, richer and more comprehensive information can be captured, leading to more generalized feature representations. This helps to improve the accuracy of predictions and the performance of the model. Inspired by this, we propose a multiscale feature fusion model for click-through rate prediction(3DMS-CTR). First, we propose a multi-dimensional multi-scale feature extraction algorithm, called 3DMSF. It extracts features across temporal, topological, and frequency dimensions using different scale methods to perform hierarchical feature extraction on low-order, high-order, and interest features, ensuring multigranularity in feature learning. Then, we employ a multi-scale feature fusion method based on an improved attention mechanism, called MS2F. During the multi-scale feature fusion process, the weights of different features are dynamically adjusted, thereby enhancing the effectiveness and robustness of feature representations. Finally, inspired by collaborative filtering techniques, we propose a low-order, high-order, and interest feature-based collaborative graph-enhanced embedding method, called LHI2gra. This method addresses the issues of feature sparsity and missing features. Experiments show that this model effectively extracts multi-scale features. On three public datasets, our model outperforms the baseline.
item.authors: Sirui Duan;Hui Le;Qiwen Li;Rong Wang;Tun Li;Yunpeng Xiao;

item.title: CGAD: A Cross-Granularity Aware Framework for Time Series Anomaly Detection
item.description: Unsupervised time series anomaly detection is vital for industrial system reliability, yet remains challenging due to complex temporal dynamics and diverse anomalies across granularities. One major difficulty lies in capturing global temporal dependencies to detect continuous sequence anomalies while maintaining sensitivity to localized point anomalies. In this paper, we propose CGAD, a cross-granularity aware framework that explicitly integrates window-level contrastive learning and point-level reconstruction to detect both sequence and point anomalies within a unified architecture. At the core of CGAD is a Temporal Compression–Expansion (TCE) module that compresses each window into a compact representation for contrast and expands it to the original resolution for reconstruction, enabling end-to-end interaction between coarse- and fine-grained temporal patterns. Furthermore, CGAD employs a global reference center with a quadruplet contrastive loss to enhance global discrimination, and a Huber-NLL loss to ensure robust local reconstruction against noise. Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets demonstrate that CGAD outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by detecting both point and sequence anomalies effectively, achieving up to 18.56% relative improvement with higher computational efficiency.
item.authors: Zhibin Zhang;Xiaohong Zhang;Tao Yin;Meichen Jiang;Chun Huang;Meng Yan;

item.title: Cross-Modal Inconsistent Information-Based Network for Fake News Detection
item.description: The rapid advancement of social media platforms has significantly reduced the cost of information dissemination, yet it has also led to a proliferation of fake news, posing a threat to societal trust and credibility. Most of fake news detection research focused on integrating text and image information to represent the consistency of multiple modes in news content, while paying less attention to inconsistent information. Besides, existing methods that leveraged inconsistent information often caused one mode overshadowing another, leading to ineffective use of inconsistent clue. To address these issues, we propose a cross-modal inconsistent feature fusion network (CIFF-Net). Inspired by human judgment processes for determining truth and falsity in news, CIFF-Net focuses on inconsistent parts when news content is generally consistent and consistent parts when it is generally inconsistent. Specifically, CIFF-Net extracts semantic and global features from images and texts respectively, and learns consistency information between modes through a multiple feature fusion module. To deal with the problem of modal information being easily masked, we design a single modal feature filtering strategy to capture inconsistent information from corresponding modes separately. Finally, similarity scores are calculated based on global features with adaptive adjustments made to achieve weighted fusion of consistent and inconsistent features. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that CIFF-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods across public fake news datasets derived from real social medias.
item.authors: Aohan Li;Jiaxin Chen;Dengyong Zhang;Yuling Liu;Yihui Luo;Xin Liao;

item.title: Dynamic Ensemble Active Learning for Drifting Imbalanced Data Streams
item.description: Concept drift and class imbalance are two critical challenges in data stream analysis, often interrelated in their effects. Concept drift can intensify the impact of class imbalance, while class imbalance can impede the detection and management of concept drift. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel semi-supervised classification approach, Dynamic Ensemble Active Learning for Drifting Imbalanced Data Streams (DEAL-DI). DEAL-DI employs a hybrid dynamic labeling strategy that combines an uncertainty threshold with a random selection mechanism. By dynamically adjusting the threshold based on the current imbalance ratio, this strategy effectively identifies the most informative instances, thereby reducing labeling costs. Additionally, a comprehensive imbalance-handling strategy is proposed, focusing on minority class samples not only during the creation of new classifiers but also by reusing minority instances at the sample level. A novel dynamic subensemble method is further developed to select the top-performing classifiers under current conditions, ensuring their inclusion in subsequent predictions and enhancing model performance. Extensive experiments on both real-world and synthetic data streams demonstrate that DEAL-DI significantly improves recall and G-mean compared to other semi-supervised methods, while simultaneously reducing labeling costs.
item.authors: Kaixiang Yang;Yi Zhang;Zhiwen Yu;Jia-Nan Liu;Tong Zhang;C. L. Philip Chen;

item.title: Progressive Optimization Network for Open Vocabulary Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization
item.description: Open vocabulary temporal action localization (OVTAL) aims to utilize prior knowledge learned from seen action categories to detect unseen ones. However, existing methods often struggle with inaccurate alignment between visual features and class semantics, significantly limiting model performance, especially when addressing novel action categories. Improving the alignment quality of the visual and text information is a key challenge in OVTAL. Therefore, this paper proposes a progressive optimization network (PONet) with single timestamp supervision to enhance the model’s ability to recognize and localize novel action categories. Specifically, PONet employs semantic-guided early enhancement for initial feature screening, effectively strengthening class-relevant visual information while suppressing irrelevant noise. Building on this, context-semantic late enhancement is introduced to jointly model visual features from both temporal and semantic channels, hierarchically optimizing visual-semantic alignment and improving category discrimination of visual representations. Finally, pseudo-label constraints are utilized to refine action boundaries, significantly improving the accuracy and robustness of action localization. Extensive experiments on THUMOS14 and ActivityNet1.3 datasets demonstrate that PONet effectively reduces reliance on fully labeled data while enhancing the integrity and accuracy of action localization in open vocabulary scenarios, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
item.authors: Jing Wang;Dehui Kong;Jinghua Li;Xiaochen Wang;Baocai Yin;

item.title: Causal Intention Alignment for Representation Optimization in Trust and Interest Joint Prediction
item.description: Social Networking Services (SNSs) serve as platforms where users engage in both social behaviors (build trust relationships) and consumption behaviors (express interests). Joint modeling of these two types of behavior enables a more comprehensive understanding of user preferences and relationships, which can facilitate applications such as personalized recommendations and online social services. However, previous studies often overlook the underlying intentions behind user behaviors, which may amplify the optimization errors caused by intention misalignment. Moreover, user representations involved in the two prediction tasks are typically integrated through a predefined linear strategy during representation sharing or fusion, which limits the ability of the model to achieve an adaptive balance state for better optimization. To this end, we propose a causality-driven joint prediction framework Intention Alignment and Mutual Information for Joint Modeling (IAMI4JM) to mitigate these issues. Specifically, we mine user intentions from both social and consumption behavior perspectives, and align these behavioral intentions to mitigate the amplification of optimization errors caused by intention bias in the original data. Based on this, we further design a joint framework to effectively model the interplay between the two behaviors. Besides, we leverage mutual information to flexibly adjust the balance state among representations under the fusion strategy, thereby enhancing the training process and overall performance. Finally, experimental results on three real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the IAMI4JM.
item.authors: Junwei Li;Jiatian Chen;Lei Chen;Xingyu Lu;Yulu Du;Le Wu;Richang Hong;Weisheng Li;

item.title: ClueKGC: Clue-Augmented Prompting for Knowledge Graph Completion
item.description: Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) is a crucial task aimed at enhancing the completeness and accuracy of Knowledge Graph (KG) by filling in missing information. However, existing KGC methods face several significant challenges. 1) Entity Conflict Issue: during the training phase, positive and negative samples exhibit high similarity in explicit structural feature embedding (ESFE), making it difficult to distinguish between similar entities. 2) Inductive Reasoning Issue: during the inference phase, most models typically use implicit memorization methods, perform poorly when dealing with multi-hop relations. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Clue-Augmented method called ClueKGC, which provides the CrsKGE module for Entity Conflict Issue and the MRA module for the Inductive Inference Issue. CrsKGE first utilizes Negative Clues to narrow the score difference between positive and negative samples, and prompts the model to identify potential False Negatives, thereby alleviating the impact of False Negatives. Subsequently, the CrsKGE leverages Feature Clues often overlooked by most methods, to prompt the model to learn implicit structural feature embedding (ISFE) of KG, thereby increasing the distinctiveness between entities and ultimately resolving the Entity Conflict Issue. MRA utilizes meta-path mining to extract additional information about entities and relations as Answer Clues for answer prompting. Extensive experiments on the FB15K-237 and WN18RR datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method. Notably, compared to the strongest baselines, ClueKGC improves the MRR metric by 6.47% on FB15K-237, while also achieving a highly competitive MRR of 0.500 on WN18RR.
item.authors: Xin Zhang;Wuyang Zhang;Jie Chen;Shu Zhao;

item.title: Mining High Utility Patterns Under Guidance
item.description: Frequent Pattern Mining (FPM) plays a crucial role in, e.g., social analytics. However, FPM faces the challenge of striking a balance between the computational cost and results quality. To address the issue, we investigate the problem of high utility patterns mining under guidance and propose a comprehensive approach to the issue. We first introduce a utility function, that integrates the support metric with pattern size to assess the utility value of a pattern. We then develop a distributed mining algorithm GiMiner, that relies on a guidance network to mine high utility patterns. In particular, the guidance network, that is built up through calculating prior probability among structurally related patterns on a (small sample) graph guides the pattern expansion. By incorporating time constraint, GiMiner tackles the FPM task in a flexible way, well balancing the computational cost and result quality. As verified via experimental studies, our algorithms are of superior effectiveness as well as efficiency, compared with existing state-of-the-art methods on real-life graphs.
item.authors: Xin Wang;Xing Jiang;Jie-Jun Zou;Bin Chen;Ji Zhang;Wen-Bo Xie;

item.title: MixDPT: Robust Prompt Fine-Tuning via Multi-Group Prompting and Matrix Decomposition-Reconstruction
item.description: The hyperparameter search for the optimal prompt length requires a significant amount of computing resources, and the method of fixing the prompt length in practical applications degrades performance across tasks, severely limiting the potential of large language models (LLMs) and large vision-language models (LVLMs). To address this issue, we propose a multi-group prompt fine-tuning method with matrix decomposition (MixDPT), which mainly consists of two modules: the Adaptive Multi-Group Prompt (AMP) module and the Matrix Decomposition-Reconstruction (MDR) module. Specifically, the AMP module divides the prompt length in LLMs into three fixed groups with simple, medium, and difficult tasks so as to isolate the task types and reduce the interference among the features. Furthermore, to efficiently adjust the model’s attention weights under computational resource constraints, we embed the MDR module, a multi-head low-rank matrix, into the Wq, Wk, and Wv weight matrices within the first Transformer layers of a frozen large model. This allows us to effectively reshape the attention weights while keeping the main body of the large model frozen, thereby significantly enhancing the model’s feature representation capability. Finally, extensive experiments on various language tasks, including SuperGLUE, NER, QA, and SRL, as well as FGVC in LVLMs demonstrate that the proposed MixDPT significantly improves the performance of prompt-based models and achieves superior performance at the same prompt length, significantly improving its stability and generalization with fixed 140-token prompts.
item.authors: Yun Ding;Jin Zhu;Gengsheng Zhang;Yansen Su;Chunhou Zheng;

item.title: Center Contrastive Long-Tailed Hashing for Unsupervised Remote Sensing Image Retrieval
item.description: Remote sensing image retrieval plays a vital role in geospatial analysis, environmental monitoring, and land-use classification. However, existing hash-based retrieval methods are typically supervised and assume balanced category distributions, which rarely hold in real-world remote sensing scenarios. In practice, remote sensing imagery often exhibits a long-tailed distribution, where a few dominant categories (head classes) contain abundant samples while many categories (tail classes) are severely underrepresented. This imbalance biases representation learning toward majority classes and significantly degrades retrieval performance for minority categories, making it difficult to learn discriminative hash representations for tail classes. To address this issue, we propose an unsupervised retrieval framework termed Center Contrastive Long-tailed Hashing (CCLH). The proposed method extracts semantic features using a pre-trained Vision Transformer and discovers latent semantic structures via unsupervised clustering. Based on the obtained clusters, we project cluster centers into the hash space via a shared hashing encoder to generate center hash codes, which are used to guide representation learning without requiring manual annotations. We further introduce a center-guided contrastive learning strategy that aligns image hash codes with their corresponding semantic centers while separating them from others, thereby reducing bias toward head classes and improving representation learning for tail categories. Extensive experiments on synthetic long-tailed benchmarks and a real-world remote sensing dataset demonstrate that CCLH consistently outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised hashing methods, validating its effectiveness and robustness under imbalanced retrieval scenarios.
item.authors: Yuan Cao;Yifan Sun;Zifan Liu;Zuojin Huang;Jie Gui;Yanwei Yu;

item.title: Geometric Ensembles for Machine Translation
item.description: We propose Geometric Ensembles, a framework for ensembling neural machine translation (NMT) systems that operates entirely in output space: given multiple candidate translations (with no access to model weights), we exploit discrete (combinatorial) metric geometry to select an aggregate hypothesis. The resulting ensemble is black-box, parallelizable, and runs on a commodity CPU at every pool size we tested, using two to three orders of magnitude less memory than the white-box (standard) ensemble, which saturates a 40 GiB A100 by $N=25$N=25. Across four MT benchmarks the framework matches or exceeds the standard ensemble, and the same geometric perspective yields an interpretable account of standard NMT ensemble behavior: in the overwhelming majority of test cases, its output is the geometric center of the candidate translations.
item.authors: Hafiz Asif;Nathaniel Hobbs;Periklis A. Papakonstantinou;Jaideep Vaidya;Jia Xu;

item.title: A Dual-Preference Personalized Route Recommendation Method Inspired by Information Propagation Structures
item.description: Personalized route recommendation is one of the core tasks of intelligent transportation systems. How to achieve explicit decoupling and collaborative optimization of user preferences and cost preferences under external traffic feature constraints is a key scientific issue for improving the effectiveness of personalized route recommendations. To address this problem, this paper proposes a user-cost dual-preference personalized route recommendation method inspired by the information propagation structure. Firstly, traffic checkpoints are encoded as trajectory nodes. Consecutive transfers between checkpoints are represented as travel directions. Multiple route combinations under the same origin-destination condition are treated as route-choice uncertainty. BERT is then used to capture users’ historical behavioral preferences. Secondly, an adaptive graph convolutional network is adopted. It learns cost sensitivity from distance, estimated travel time, and road network structure. Finally, an inter-layer attention mechanism is designed. It enables interactive optimization of the two types of preferences under external traffic constraints. Experiments on vehicle trajectory datasets from Beijing and Porto show that the proposed method achieves F1-scores of 0.859, 0.798, and 0.751 on short-, medium-, and long-trajectory tasks, respectively, on the Beijing dataset. The results are significantly better than those of existing baseline methods.
item.authors: Rong Wang;Sihuai Peng;Yutang Liang;Pingfeng Zhong;Chaolong Jia;Tun Li;

item.title: Disentangled Representation Learning for Multi-Modal Multi-Domain Fake News Detection
item.description: With the development of artificial intelligence, multi-modal and multi-domain fake news detection have attracted increasing attention due to their ability to integrate information from different modalities and adapt to diverse scenarios in different domains. Existing methods face a core challenge when handling multi-domain fake news detection, since they struggle to efficiently extract and clearly distinguish between domain-specific and domain-shared features. This blurred boundary not only disrupts the balance between the model’s specialization and generalization, but also directly leads to feature redundancy, limiting performance improvement. To address this challenge, we propose a Disentangled Representation learning based Multi-modal Multi-domain Fake News Detection framework (DRMMFND), which effectively analyzes and separates features by different modalities and domains, thereby improving the accuracy of detection. This framework utilizes three mixture of adapters networks to fuse multi-modal information, integrating both domain-specific and domain-shared expert adapters. It uses a router equipped with learnable prompts and a Top-K strategy to generate various types of domain outputs. Furthermore, an auxiliary loss and an orthogonal loss are introduced, achieving effective decoupling of domain information and reducing information redundancy between domains. We conduct experiments on the Weibo, Weibo21 and FineFake datasets, and experimental results show that this approach improves performance in most multi-domain scenarios.
item.authors: Ying Guo;Yuan Li;Jie Liu;Qi Wang;Yong-jin Liu;

item.title: Enhancing Contrastive Learning on Learnable Graph Augmentation
item.description: Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) has become an effective paradigm in graph representation learning by establishing contrastive relationships between nodes. Existing methods typically generate positive samples through manually designed graph data augmentation and obtain negative samples via random sampling. Suboptimal augmentation can corrupt the original graph topology, while false-negative samples introduce noise that degrades node representation quality. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel graph contrastive representation learning framework called Enhancing Contrastive Learning with Augmentation (ECLA). First, we adopt a learnable augmentation module that generates adaptive augmented views through learnable edge weight adjustments. Second, we propose a joint metric method that integrates graph structural similarity and node feature similarity to model the deep semantic relationships between nodes, and based on this, we construct the distribution of positive and negative samples. Furthermore, we introduce a dual-weight contrastive loss function that enhances the contrastive learning intensity of semantically similar nodes through positive sample weights, while suppressing the negative impact of potential false-negative nodes through negative sample weights. ECLA jointly optimizes graph augmentation and representation learning in an end-to-end manner. Evaluations across diverse datasets show that ECLA consistently surpasses both leading graph contrastive methods and semi-supervised GNN baselines on node classification under severely limited label conditions.
item.authors: Yu Xu;Guixiang Zhu;Huijia Li;Jie Cao;Darko Vukovic;

item.title: Diffusion Contrastive Learning Model for Multi-Behavior Recommendation
item.description: Multi-behavior recommendation leverages diverse user interactions to capture personalized user preferences. To alleviate the data sparsity of the crucial target behavior, multi-behavior contrastive learning (MBCL) improves performance by enriching self-supervised signals from auxiliary behaviors. However, existing methods rely on heuristic augmentation techniques to construct contrastive views, which disrupt essential multi-behavior collaborative information; simultaneously, auxiliary behaviors, influenced by multiple confounders, easily introduce semantic confusion into the MBCL alignment process. Inspired by recent advances of diffusion models, we propose DiffMB, a novel diffusion contrastive learning framework. DiffMB first employs a Multi-Behavior Weight-Enhanced Graph Neural Network to capture behavioral heterogeneity through parallel encoding. At the core of DiffMB is a Hybrid Contrastive Learning (HCL) strategy that tackles this dilemma via two synergistic components. First, Target-Behavior Diffusion Contrastive Learning leverages a diffusion process to generate high-quality, semantically consistent views for the target behavior, thereby consolidating its semantics while avoiding the disruption of collaborative information. Second, Multi-Behavior Collaborative Contrastive Learning extracts valuable collaborative signals from auxiliary behaviors. Furthermore, a Dynamic Optimization Strategy is introduced to reconcile gradient conflicts in multi-task training. Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate that DiffMB significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
